properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony 2026-10-30, on dec:idea-fold-and-removal-candidates-from-the-2026-10-30-counts, in his words: "could we make a snapshot now and make the changes now (including the deletions). As I'm the main user, if any of these are missing, I'll be the one to notice. Then come December, if we're missing something we can restore only what is 'missing'."

This reopens part of an accepted rule: dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first asks for evidence from more than one person's projects AND a refusing-stub release first. His idea replaces "evidence across projects" with "the main user's own use, then restore what's missed".

OPTIONS (none chosen):
A. HIS IDEA AS SAID — tag a snapshot (a release tag is one already), make the seven folds, the renames, and the deletions of the 8 report candidates in the next release; in December restore, from the snapshot, only the tools found missing.
B. STUB NOW, DELETE IN DECEMBER — the same changes now, but each removed name stays as a refusing stub for one release: a call to it changes nothing and answers with the tool that replaced it (or "retired 2026-10-30 — say if you needed this"), and every stub call is counted in the usage ledger. In December, delete the stubs nobody called and restore the ones somebody did. This is his idea with "noticed missing" made a count instead of a memory; it meets the accepted rule's stub clause and amends only its across-projects clause.
C. FOLDS NOW, REMOVALS LATER — make the seven folds now (a twin already carries each job, so nothing is lost), and leave the 40 never-reached tools, including the 8 report candidates, for a findable path and a re-count before any is judged.

COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside the idea:
1. Absence is mostly silent. An agent meets the tool list, not the person: a tool that is not listed raises no error, and the agent works around it with another tool or by hand and says nothing. The only failure anyone sees is a call BY NAME from a skill, a prompt or a script. So "restore what's missing" can only restore what something called — and the never-reached tools are exactly the ones nothing calls. A refusing stub (B) is what turns a silent absence into a counted call.
2. He is the main user, not the only one: about 6% of flo2.io calls in the 2026-10-30 count are other people's (Alex uses reflow2 over MCP; others use flo2.io). The accepted rule that reflow2's MCP stays as-is promises them a deprecating release before a removal. A, done without a stub release, breaks that promise; B keeps it.
3. Size: A and B are about the same build now — each removal also edits the served skills, flo2's skill text and doors that name the tool, the tests, and the docs site. B adds a few lines per stub plus one December clean-up. C is the smallest. Restoring under A is cheap when the snapshot is a tag (one revert per tool).
4. Step 6 (the named cue message) compares cues like for like; changing the surface first moves the baseline a little. The folds touch few cued tools, so this is minor.

properties.name: SETTLED 2026-10-30 (B) — the fold and removal candidates are retired now as counted refusing stubs for one release; in December the stubs nobody called are deleted and the ones somebody called are restored
properties.rationale: Anthony's brainstorm on step 7's proposal 2, 2026-10-30. The agent's finding (a ranking, not a decision): B gets what he asked for — the changes made now, his own use as the test — while making 'missing' measured rather than noticed and keeping the promise to MCP users; C is the cheapest.
